note: How look/run capture the working tree and, crucially, what a grep records. worldstate.rs: every observation carries a Marker { root, state } where root is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolved per-observation from the path the observation touched (canonicalized; NO_GIT outside a repo), and state hashes HEAD plus `git diff HEAD --binary`. observe.rs look_grep: (a) it passes -H unconditionally so single-file greps key on a real filename; (b) a ZERO-match grep records one NoMatch entry whose key is resolve_key(search root) and whose label is "no-match: <pattern> in <root>", with the marker resolved from the search root; (c) a grep WITH matches records one GrepMatch entry per matched file, keyed on the matched file's resolved path with label "<file> (grep: <pattern>)", and the SEARCH ROOT IS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE in those entries — the comment says explicitly "keyed by that file's resolved path (fix 2), not by the search root or the grep command line". So for a positive-match grep, nothing captured distinguishes a repo-wide search from a single-file search that happened to match the same files. look_path records the opened file's key/label and per-file marker; run records key=cmdline, label "proc: <cmdline> (exit N)", marker from the process cwd.

What survives from an observation into a fact and its snapshot. pending.rs: PendingEntry carries kind (ObservationKind: Path | GrepMatch | NoMatch | Proc), key, label, output, world_root, world_state, captured_at. facts.rs mint(): the fold copies ONLY key, label, world_root, world_state into ExtentEntry — the kind is dropped, and a grep's pattern exists nowhere except inside the display label text ("no-match: <pattern> in <root>", "<file> (grep: <pattern>)"). Two schema-evolution precedents matter for extending this: (a) world_root is #[serde(default)] for entries minted before it existed, and an empty root is deliberately read as "comparable with nothing" — "check treats it that way rather than guessing"; (b) facts.jsonl ships in the snapshot with full extent entries (mint_windows reads the snapshot's facts.jsonl, and its doc says the Create timestamp "ships in facts.jsonl, and the snapshot copies refusals.log beside it"). Also: there is deliberately no flag on fact's surface that lets a caller supply extent or captured output — "that absence is the guarantee that a fact was actually backed by a look/run". Extent, output and pin are set once at mint and no revision event can carry them.

How a memo is assembled and what render refuses today. compose.rs render(): prose blocks in order, then an appended "## Evidence ledger" table (one row per non-withdrawn claim, Status always OWED, no Domain/Extent columns — v1's Domain ⊆ Extent was retired on evidence and deriving scope from facts' extents "would recreate exactly the vacuity that measurement rejected"), then a "## Facts" table (ID, Note, Extent-as-captured labels, Rests under). Structured tables rendered from fields are the established shape; only labels are rendered, never absolute keys ("a committed document should not carry /Users/<someone>/..."). main.rs Render arm (lines 640-700): compose::render, then write document, then snapshot::write (document first so a failed snapshot leaves a recoverable state), then a pending-observations warning that is explicitly "Warned, never refused: an author may have deliberately looked at something they chose not to cite". Nothing in the render path refuses on the content of the workspace today. One drift precedent recorded in the comments: the CLI arm used to mint the workspace identity and the MCP render handler did not, so a memo authored over MCP shipped without one — the fix moved the act into snapshot::write, the one shared place.

The project's refusal doctrine and where TET-28 already sits in the roadmap. README Constraints: "Refusals are format-level, never heuristic. 'You did not point at your evidence' is a decidable question. 'This looks wrong' is not, and belongs in the human-owed partition or nowhere." Two partitions, never a single document-level verdict; machine-checked failures are the grammar/subset/abutting/unsettled/cascade/ledger/verdict/out-of-proof/provenance-drift set; human-owed "none of it is settled by a passing check, and none of it fails the run". note: Confirmed against the record types themselves: tetel has no notion of a recommendation, and no kind or class on either record a memo is made of. claims.rs: a Claim is { id, prop, from (cited fact ids), withdrawn, revisions } and ClaimEvent::Create carries only id/prop/from/timestamp — a proposition resting on facts, nothing typing what kind of proposition it is. prose.rs: a Block is { id, heading, level, text, cite, revisions } — prose "is where the author talks, not where they're audited", creation is deliberately ungated, and the only structure a block carries is heading-ness, depth, text and claim citations. Nothing on either surface marks a claim or a paragraph as a recommendation, an instruction, or anything else. Also relevant precedents captured here: claim refuses without --cites and on unknown fact ids (so citing-a-real-record refusals are the established authoring shape), and prose.rs documents the --before insertion design and the append-only revise-with-why discipline.

scope.rs's "Language-agnostic by construction" section, verbatim where load-bearing: "Tetel documents systems in any language, so nothing here may be tuned to one. There is no list of languages and no list of extensions." What counts as a filename is decided by shape rules plus a vocabulary of extensions the workspace has actually opened, "read out of the captured extents"; the rejected alternative — "a hard-coded map from extension to language" — is "exactly the coupling this avoids". So the project's stated construction rule is that no check may require parsing or knowledge specific to one programming language; anything that would (e.g. parsing call expressions to extract argument values) is the coupling the doctrine exists to exclude.
